source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
injuries.short_comment: Antetokounmpo (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.long_comment: Antetokounmpo previously dealt with a wrist injury in November, and he's now working through a groin issue that puts his status for Sunday's game up in the air. He has yet to miss a game this season, but if he's not cleared to play against Oklahoma City, then Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis would be the top candidates to enter Miami's starting lineup.

injuries.name: Myron Gardner
injuries.short_comment: Gardner (hamstring) is probable for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
injuries.long_comment: The probable tag suggests Gardner is on the verge of returning to the hardwood after a one-game absence due to injury. He's been in and out of the starting five, but he started his last three games before missing Wednesday's win over the Bucks. He's averaging 3.0 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game this season, so even if he's cleared to play Sunday, he shouldn't carry a ton of fantasy appeal.

injuries.name: Alex Caruso
injuries.short_comment: Caruso (hip) won't play Sunday against the Heat.
injuries.long_comment: Sunday will mark Caruso's second straight game on the sidelines, but maybe he'll be able to get back out there for Monday's meeting in Indiana. Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford will help pick up the slack in Caruso's absence.

injuries.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
injuries.short_comment: Gilgeous-Alexander (back/neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus Miami.
injuries.long_comment: After scoring 40 points in Friday's 126-120 win over the Pelicans, Gilgeous-Alexander could miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign due to back and neck issues. With Nikola Topic (hip), Alex Caruso (hip) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) all unavailable, Bennett Stirtz may be needed in the starting lineup if Gilgeous-Alexander is ruled out Sunday.

injuries.name: Jaylin Williams
injuries.short_comment: Williams (back) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Miami.
injuries.long_comment: Williams missed seven consecutive contests due to back spasms. He has since appeared in the Thunder's last two games. However, the 24-year-old won't suit up Sunday against the Heat, the first game of a back-to-back for Oklahoma City. Without Williams on the floor, Aday Mara, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy could see more minutes.

injuries.name: Chet Holmgren
injuries.short_comment: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injuries.long_comment: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injuries.name: Jalen Williams
injuries.short_comment: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

injuries.name: Cason Wallace
injuries.short_comment: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injuries.long_comment: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injuries.name: Thomas Sorber
injuries.short_comment: Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
injuries.long_comment: Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

injuries.name: Nikola Topic
injuries.short_comment: Topic (hip) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Heat.
injuries.long_comment: Topic has appeared in only three games for Oklahoma City this season. He will now miss a second consecutive contest due to a hip injury, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday versus the Pacers. Considering Topic has averaged just 11.3 minutes per outing, his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation, though he might have seen more action if Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back/neck), who is questionable, can't suit up.
